newsitem.title: GERMANY: German tour operator NUR profits down, sales up.
newsitem.headline: German tour operator NUR profits down, sales up.

text.p: Leading tour operator NUR Touristic said it expected to grow faster than the depressed German package holiday market this year with a seven percent rise in sales and turnover.
Overall demand in the German travel market remained troubled by the difficult economic situation and high unemployment, the Karstadt AG subsidiary said.
NUR group pre-tax profits fell nearly eight percent to 85.7 million marks in the 1995-96 year due to tough competition for its travel agency chain and a decline in cruises, a statement said.
Holiday sales by its German, Belgian, Dutch and Austrian units rose 9.5 percent to 4.9 million passengers and turnover grew nine percent to 4.85 billion marks.
In Germany, pre-tax profits fell 13 percent to 53.1 million marks despite a 10.6 percent rise to 3.3 million holidays sold and 7.2 percent increase in turnover to 3.6 billion marks.
The second-largest German tour operator behind TUI added that it improved its market share last year.
NUR said it maintained its market leadership in Belgium, won market share in Austria and improved profits in the Netherlands.
The tour operator sells mostly charter holidays to short-haul tourist destinations using airlines such as Deutsche Lufthansa AG subsidiary Condor, Hapag-Lloyd and Aero Lloyd.
Long-haul seat capacity is purchased from a range of carriers, including Delta Air Lines, South African Airways SAA.CN, Singapore Airlines and Thai Airways .
